title: Commiphora africana Ethanol Extract Attenuates Inflammatory Responses With Reduced NF-kappaB/AP-1 Activation and Src/TAK1-Related Signaling Changes.
authors: Mou, Canglang; Wang, Yuhao; Huang, Lei; Su, Jinghan; You, Long; He, Ziliang; Hu, Yeye; Wei, Weizhaole; Choi, Wooram; Lee, Byoung-Hee; Bang, Woo Young; Byun, Hye-Woo; Lee, Jongsung; Kim, Ji Hye; Cho, Jae Youl
one_liner_zh: 研究非洲没药乙醇提取物的抗炎机制，涉及NF-kB/AP-1信号通路和Src/TAK1分子对接，但核心是植物药理学而非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅分子对接为边缘方法。
abstract: BACKGROUND: The bark, resin, and roots of Commiphora africana (A. Rich.) Engl. have traditionally been used in African medicine to treat fever, stomach disorders, colic, and swelling. However, despite this traditional use, its anti-inflammatory activity and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We evaluated the anti-inflammatory activity of C. africana ethanol extract (Caf-EE) in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated macrophages and in murine models of HCl/EtOH-induced acute gastric mucosal injury and LPS-induced acute lung injury. Reporter assays, gene expression analysis, immunoblotting, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS)-guided compound annotation, network pharmacology, and molecular docking were used to investigate the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of Caf-EE. RESULTS: Caf-EE inhibited nitrite production without cytotoxicity in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. GC-MS-guided feature annotation identified representative candidate constituents of Caf-EE, and network pharmacology indicated their association with inflammation-related pathways. Mechanistically, Caf-EE suppressed MyD88- and TRIF-mediated NF-kappaB/Activator protein 1 (AP-1) transcriptional activity and reduced the expression of inflammatory genes. Caf-EE also inhibited phosphorylation of Src/IkappaB kinase (IKK)/IkappaB- and Transforming growth factor-beta-activated kinase 1 (TAK1)/c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK)/c-Jun-associated signaling proteins and increased the thermal stability of Src and TAK1. In vivo, Caf-EE attenuated HCl/EtOH-induced acute gastric mucosal injury and LPS-induced acute lung injury, accompanied by reduced phosphorylation of Src and TAK1 in both tissues. Among the representative GC-MS-annotated compounds, 9,19-cyclolanost-24-en-3-ol exhibited the highest predicted binding affinity for Src and TAK1 in molecular docking analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, this study provides mechanistic evidence for the anti-inflammatory effects of Caf-EE through modulation of Src/TAK1-associated signaling. Furthermore, the protective effects observed in acute inflammatory disease models support the further development of Caf-EE as a therapeutic candidate for inflammatory disorders.
abstract_zh: 背景：非洲没药（*Commiphora africana* (A. Rich.) Engl.）的树皮、树脂和根在非洲医学中传统上用于治疗发热、胃部疾病、绞痛和肿胀。然而，尽管有这种传统用途，其抗炎活性及潜在分子机制仍鲜有表征。方法：我们评估了非洲没药乙醇提取物（Caf-EE）在脂多糖（LPS）刺激的巨噬细胞以及HCl/EtOH诱导的急性胃黏膜损伤和LPS诱导的急性肺损伤小鼠模型中的抗炎活性。采用报告基因检测、基因表达分析、免疫印迹、细胞热位移分析（CETSA）、气相色谱-质谱联用（GC-MS）引导的化合物注释、网络药理学和分子对接来研究Caf-EE的抗炎机制。结果：Caf-EE在LPS刺激的RAW264.7巨噬细胞中抑制亚硝酸盐产生且无细胞毒性。GC-MS引导的特征注释识别了Caf-EE的代表性候选成分，网络药理学表明它们与炎症相关通路有关联。机制上，Caf-EE抑制了MyD88和TRIF介导的NF-kappaB/激活蛋白1（AP-1）转录活性，并降低了炎症基因的表达。Caf-EE还抑制了Src/IkappaB激酶（IKK）/IkappaB-和转化生长因子-β激活激酶1（TAK1）/c-Jun N末端激酶（JNK）/c-Jun相关信号蛋白的磷酸化，并增加了Src和TAK1的热稳定性。在体内，Caf-EE减轻了HCl/EtOH诱导的急性胃黏膜损伤和LPS诱导的急性肺损伤，伴随两种组织中Src和TAK1磷酸化的降低。在代表性的GC-MS注释化合物中，9,19-环羊毛甾-24-烯-3-醇在分子对接分析中对Src和TAK1表现出最高的预测结合亲和力。结论：总体而言，本研究为Caf-EE通过调节Src/TAK1相关信号发挥抗炎作用提供了机制证据。此外，在急性炎症疾病模型中观察到的保护效应支持Caf-EE作为炎症性疾病治疗候选药物的进一步开发。
